summary: beginner/life-line.md's empirical section names three studies (Newrick et al. 1990, Wilson & Mather 1974, Lucas et al. 2019) but its source footer named only Lucas et al. Verified the other two by targeted lookup -- Newrick, Affie & Corrall (1990), J R Soc Med 83(8):499-501, 100 autopsies, significant correlation; Wilson & Mather (1974), JAMA 229(11):1421-1422 (letter), 51 cadavers, no correlation -- and added both to the footer. Reworded 04-life-line.mdx's lesson-takeaway sentence 'it has not held up under testing' (flagged open since PP-RELAY-011) to 'the studies that have directly tested it find no reliable relationship between line length and lifespan', matching the mixed-but-net-unsupportive record already stated accurately elsewhere in the same lesson/article rather than implying a uniform negative result. No new studies, claims, or palmistry interpretations introduced. Updated docs/CURRENT_STATE.md and added Pass 6 to docs/source-verification-log.md.
